sections.h2: How do I sell my house fast in West Allis, Wisconsin?
sections.html:
Start by deciding whether you want a financed buyer, a buyer you find yourself, or a cash purchase, then line up the Wisconsin paperwork that every sale needs. In West Allis that means a real estate condition report for the buyer, an electronic transfer return filed with the state, and a deed recorded with the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds. A buyer who does not rely on a mortgage removes the loan and appraisal steps, which is where listings usually lose time.

West Allis is a Milwaukee County suburb and the eleventh most populous city in Wisconsin. The Census Bureau estimates 60,119 residents as of July 1, 2025, compared with 60,325 in the 2020 census. It covers 11.38 square miles of land, with 5,300.5 residents per square mile.

sections.h2: What is the housing stock like in West Allis?
sections.html:
West Allis is a dense city, and the numbers show a market of modestly priced homes with many renters. The Census Bureau reports a 55.5 percent owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024, a median owner-occupied home value of $203,800 and 28,311 households averaging 2.08 people. Median gross rent is $1,007, median household income is $67,611 in 2024 dollars, and 89.1 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

The 2020 census counted 29,015 housing units, 5.2 percent of them vacant. Wikipedia reports a homeowner vacancy rate of 1.3 percent and a rental vacancy rate of 4.9 percent. About 39.5 percent of households are one person living alone.

  • Median owner costs with a mortgage: $1,503 a month. Without a mortgage: $681.
  • Persons in poverty: 11.5 percent.
  • Language other than English spoken at home: 14.2 percent.
  • Mean travel time to work: 21.0 minutes.

sections.h2: How did West Allis become the city it is today?
sections.html:
The city is named for Edward P. Allis, whose Milwaukee manufacturing company became Allis-Chalmers in 1901. In 1902 the company built a large plant west of its existing one in an area then called North Greenfield, and before the 1880s the same ground had been known as Honey Creek. The area incorporated as the Village of West Allis and became a city in 1906.

With Allis-Chalmers as the area's largest manufacturer, West Allis became the largest suburb of Milwaukee in the early twentieth century, and its population grew fivefold between 1910 and 1930. After 1965 the company declined. Its global workforce fell from a peak of 31,000 to 13,000 by 1985, it filed for bankruptcy in 1987, and it closed its last Milwaukee office in 1999.

sections.h2: What local features affect how West Allis houses sell?
sections.html:
Location and access drive most buyer questions. Interstate 94 and Interstate 41/894 run through the city, and Milwaukee County Transit System routes 18, 28, 44U, 51, 53, 54, 56, 64, 76 and 92 serve it. Portions of the Hank Aaron State Trail run near the northern border, and since 2021 the city has had a complete streets policy for new road projects.

  • Wisconsin State Fair Park. The park, home of the annual Wisconsin State Fair, sits in West Allis along with the Milwaukee Mile, described as the world's oldest racing facility.
  • Pettit National Ice Center. It is one of only two indoor speed skating rinks in the United States.
  • Candy Cane Lane. Residents along Oklahoma and Montana Avenues between 92nd and 96th Streets have put up elaborate holiday displays since 1984, which brings bumper-to-bumper traffic on December nights and has raised over $2.2 million for the MACC Fund.
  • Schools. The West Allis-West Milwaukee School District includes 11 elementary schools, Frank Lloyd Wright, Lane and West Milwaukee intermediate schools, and West Allis Central, Nathan Hale and James E. Dottke high schools. The Wisconsin Evangelical Lutheran Synod runs two grade schools in the city.

If you list in December, be ready for the traffic around Candy Cane Lane when you schedule showings on those blocks.

sections.h2: What does Wisconsin require of a West Allis home seller?
sections.html:
A seller of a one-to-four unit home must give the buyer a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. Wisconsin Statutes chapter 709 lets a buyer who does not receive it rescind within two business days after that 10-day window and get deposits back. It excuses personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-supervised fiduciaries who have never occupied the property, and it does not apply to transfers that are exempt from the transfer fee.

The grantor pays the real estate transfer fee under s. 77.22, which is 30 cents for each $100 of value. The table shows the result at several West Allis price points.

Sale priceTransfer fee at 30 cents per $100
$150,000$450
$200,000$600
$250,000$750
$300,000$900

Source: Wis. Stat. 77.22 rate applied to each price. The register collects the fee at recording, and Wis. Stat. 77.24 sends 20 percent to the county and the balance to the state. Exemptions in s. 77.25 cover transfers by will, descent or survivorship, certain transfers between parent and child for nominal consideration, and foreclosure deeds given to a mortgage holder.

sections.h2: How do I record a West Allis deed?
sections.html:
Deeds for West Allis property are recorded at the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee. The fee is $30 per document, and the electronic transfer return receipt is required for every conveyance. Pay by cash, check or money order, because the office does not take credit or debit cards.

Recording takes three to five business days in the order received, and the original comes back by mail in one to two weeks. For help filling in the electronic return, call the Wisconsin Department of Revenue at (608) 266-1594. The register's office cannot prepare documents or give legal advice, so most sellers rely on a title company or attorney. Questions about a pending recording go to (414) 278-4005.

sections.h2: How are West Allis property taxes collected, and what if I owe back taxes?
sections.html:
West Allis taxes are billed by the city, so ask the City Treasurer for the current due dates and installment plan, and ask the City Assessor for your assessed value and property record before you list. Wisconsin assessors value property at its full value in a private sale, and your title company will work out how the current-year bill is divided at closing.

The Milwaukee County Treasurer collects delinquent property taxes for 2024 and prior years for every county municipality except the City of Milwaukee, which covers West Allis. The Treasurer's page says state law requires an 18 percent per year delinquency charge, so paying early saves money. Call (414) 278-4033 to arrange a payment plan. Online payment carries a 2.55 percent card fee or a $1.50 e-check fee, charged by the payment processor.

If you owe back taxes, ask your title company how they are paid from the proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the Treasurer before you accept an offer so the net number you compare is accurate.

sections.h2: Which sale route should a West Allis owner pick?
sections.html:
Put the options side by side and ask each buyer for written terms.

  • Agent listing. Fits a house in presentable condition when you are not rushed.
  • For sale by owner. Keeps more of the price in your pocket but leaves disclosures and negotiations to you.
  • Cash buyer. Fits houses that need repairs, inherited or tenant-occupied properties, and owners trying to avoid foreclosure. Compare the net figure after title and recording costs.

faqs.q: How quickly can a West Allis house sell?
faqs.a: Timing depends on the buyer. A buyer who does not need a loan has no approval or appraisal to wait for, so the closing date is mostly a matter of title work and recording. A financed purchase adds showings, inspections and underwriting.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Milwaukee County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $30 per document, plus the transfer fee shown on your electronic return receipt. The Register of Deeds takes cash, checks and money orders but not cards, and records documents within three to five business days.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property taxes in West Allis?
faqs.a: The Milwaukee County Treasurer collects delinquent taxes for 2024 and prior years in every county municipality except the City of Milwaukee. The state-required delinquency charge is 18 percent per year. Call (414) 278-4033 to set up a payment plan.

faqs.q: Do I need a condition report if I inherited the house?
faqs.a: Not if you are a personal representative or trustee who never occupied the property. Chapter 709 excuses those fiduciaries. A transfer by will, descent or survivorship is also exempt from the transfer fee under s. 77.25, which removes the report requirement for that transfer.

faqs.q: What is the transfer fee on a $200,000 West Allis sale?
faqs.a: The fee is $600, which is 30 cents for each $100 of value. The grantor pays it when the deed is recorded, and the electronic transfer return is filed with the Wisconsin Department of Revenue.
